correctness.rationale: The specified exchangeable triple Z has baseline group A=(one 0,two 10s), group B=(one 1,two 2s), uniformly random location of its low coordinate, with independent C-infinity jitter on (0,1/10). In the Kendall two-copy sign kernel, each within-group parent pair contributes -2/9, cross-group -1/3, giving tau(Z1,Z2)=-5/18. Within-group first/second order statistics are independent (disjoint noise coordinates) so contribute 0, while cross-group order-statistic signs are opposite, giving tau(Z_(1),Z_(2))=-1/2 and gap 2/9. Mixing 1% independent exponential triples yields C-infinity strictly positive density f>=0.01 exp(-sum x) on all positive triples. The kernel difference lies [-2,2], so total perturbation at most 4(2eta-eta²), which at eta=1/100 yields exact gap lower bound 3209/22500>0. Universal sorted-endpoint sign inequality establishes Kendall tau(min,max)>=tau(original pair) for all laws on two variables including ties, proving dimension-three minimality. Independently recalculated all fractions and 81 integer-quadruple n2 comparisons; analytic rearrangement proof is the infinite scope.
